page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.DenseIO.E6.Ax.192 is a bare-metal server in the Dense I/O family designed for storage-intensive and high-throughput enterprise workloads. The system is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs via two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 2304.0 GB of RAM, equating to 6.0 GB per logical core. High-density storage is integrated directly via 81600 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity without attached hardware GPUs.

Because this bare-metal configuration couples 384 processing threads and over two terabytes of memory with 81.6 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, it eliminates virtualization overhead and external network storage latency. The large integrated NVMe footprint offers high local input and output capability, making the instance well suited for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, big data analytics engines, and high-performance search indices. From a resource-efficiency standpoint, the server bundles substantial storage density and compute capacity into a single hardware footprint, trading off the granular scaling of smaller virtualized instances for maximum local I/O performance and physical resource isolation.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.DenseIO.E6.Ax.192 is a bare-metal Dense I/O instance built for high-throughput, I/O-heavy enterprise workloads. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 2304.0 GB, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server bundles 81600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. By combining extensive dedicated compute cores, large memory, and massive local solid-state capacity on physical hardware, BM.DenseIO.E6.Ax.192 eliminates hypervisor overhead and network storage bottlenecks. This configuration offers high resource density for big data processing, distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehousing, and real-time analytics pipelines requiring continuous, high-volume local disk input and output operations.
